landmarks.name: Bora Bora
landmarks.writeup: A famous island known for its turquoise lagoon protected by a coral reef, luxury resorts, and stunning volcanic peaks.

wiki.extract: Bora Bora is a French island group in the Leeward Islands, comprising the western part of the Society Islands of French Polynesia, an overseas collectivity of the French Republic in the South Pacific. Bora Bora has a total land area of 30.55 km2 (12 sq mi). The main island, located about 230 kilometres northwest of Papeete, is surrounded by a lagoon and a barrier reef. In the center of the island are the remnants of an extinct volcano, rising to two peaks, Mount Pahia and Mount Otemanu; the highest point is at 727 m (2,385 ft).

landmarks.name: Mount Orohena
landmarks.writeup: The highest peak in French Polynesia, located on Tahiti, offering challenging hikes and panoramic views.

wiki.extract: French Polynesia is an overseas collectivity of France and its sole overseas country; it is classified as a non-self-governing territory by the United Nations. It comprises 121 geographically dispersed islands and atolls stretching over more than 2,000 kilometres (1,200 mi) in the South Pacific Ocean. French Polynesia is associated with the European Union as an overseas country and territory (OCT). The total land area of French Polynesia is 3,521 square kilometres (1,359 sq mi), with a population of 282,596 as of September 2025 of which at least 205,000 live in the Society Islands and the remaining population lives in the rest of the archipelago.

landmarks.name: Marae Arahurahu
landmarks.writeup: An ancient Polynesian temple site on Tahiti, showcasing traditional religious architecture and cultural heritage.

wiki.extract: Maohi are the ancestors of the Polynesian peoples in Tahiti and adjacent islands.

cultural_events.name: Heiva i Tahiti
cultural_events.writeup: An annual festival celebrating Polynesian culture with traditional dance, music, and sports competitions.

cultural_events.name: Hawaiki Nui Va'a
cultural_events.writeup: A prestigious outrigger canoe race held annually between the islands of Huahine, Raiatea, and Tahaa.

food_writeup: French Polynesian cuisine blends French culinary techniques with local ingredients like seafood, tropical fruits, and taro, featuring dishes such as poisson cru (raw fish marinated in lime and coconut milk).
brief_history: Originally settled by Polynesian voyagers around 1000 BCE, French Polynesia became a French protectorate in the 19th century and remains an overseas collectivity of France with a degree of autonomy.
current_conflicts: No significant internal or external conflicts reported; political discussions focus on autonomy and independence movements.
